statement:
Prove that if $x,y,z$ are real numbers with $x+y+z=1$, then
$$x^{2}+y^{2}+z^{2}\ge\tfrac13.$$
For what values of $x,y,z$ does equality hold?
solution:
Consider
$$3(x^{2}+y^{2}+z^{2})-(x+y+z)^{2}=2x^{2}+2y^{2}+2z^{2}-2xy-2yz-2zx=(x-y)^{2}+(y-z)^{2}+(z-x)^{2}\ge0.$$
Hence $3(x^{2}+y^{2}+z^{2})\ge(x+y+z)^{2}=1$, so $x^{2}+y^{2}+z^{2}\ge\tfrac13$.
Equality holds exactly when $(x-y)^{2}=(y-z)^{2}=(z-x)^{2}=0$, i.e. $x=y=z$. Since $x+y+z=1$, equality occurs at $x=y=z=\tfrac13$.
hints: Recognise the result as a sum of squares.
Equality needs every square to be zero.
